scenes.heading: Executor Memory Tuning & Debugging OOM
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Executor Memory Tuning & Debugging OOM and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: Where OOM comes from
items: Skewed partitions too big for memory
collect() pulling data to the driver
scenes.narration: Executor out-of-memory errors usually trace back to a handful of causes. A skewed key can make one partition far too large to fit in memory, an overlarge broadcast can blow past executor capacity, and calling collect can drag a huge dataset back to the driver. Diagnosing OOM starts with identifying which of these is at play, because each has a different fix.

scenes.heading: Executor memory layout
scenes.narration: An executor's total container size is the JVM heap set by executor-memory plus a separate memoryOverhead region for off-heap and native allocations. Within the heap sit the reserved region, the unified storage-plus-execution pool, and user memory. Overhead OOM, common with Python UDFs and Arrow, means you must raise memoryOverhead, not the heap. Confusing these two is a frequent tuning mistake.

scenes.code:
spark-submit \
  --executor-memory 8g \
  --conf spark.executor.memoryOverhead=2g \
  --conf spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=800 \
  --conf spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true \
  --conf spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled=true \
  job.py
scenes.heading: Config levers against OOM
scenes.narration: Here the heap is eight gigabytes with an extra two gigabytes of overhead for off-heap and PySpark needs. Raising shuffle partitions to eight hundred makes each partition smaller so it is more likely to fit in memory. Enabling AQE and its skew-join handling lets Spark split oversized partitions automatically, attacking a common OOM root cause. These flags together cover the most frequent memory failures.

scenes.heading: Heap OOM vs overhead OOM
scenes.narration: A Java heap out-of-memory error points to partitions or cached data that are too large, so you raise executor-memory, add partitions, or fix skew. An overhead error, where YARN kills the container for exceeding physical memory, points to off-heap usage from Python workers, Arrow, or the network layer, so you raise memoryOverhead instead. Reading the exact error message tells you which region to enlarge.

scenes.heading: Driver-side OOM
items: collect() / toPandas() pull everything to the driver
scenes.narration: Not every OOM is on an executor; the driver has its own memory limits. Calling collect or toPandas drags an entire distributed dataset into the driver's heap, which is the classic driver OOM. Broadcasting many large objects or accumulating giant results does the same. The fix is to write results out or bound them with limit rather than pulling them back whole.

scenes.text: Diagnose the OOM type first; fix skew before adding RAM.
scenes.narration: Blindly increasing memory hides symptoms and wastes resources, whereas fixing skew or right-sizing partitions solves the real problem. Match the fix to the error region.
